title: Sell Mineral Rights in Diamondville, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Diamondville, WY | Lincoln Co.
metaDescription: Diamondville, WY sits next to Kemmerer's coal and trona country in Lincoln County. Get a straight read on your mineral interest, oil, gas, or otherwise.
heroLead: Diamondville sits practically on top of Kemmerer, and this corner of Lincoln County built its history on coal mining first, oil and gas leasing second, which means I always check exactly what kind of minerals your deed actually describes.
intro: The coal seams that fed Kemmerer's mines for a century sit under a lot of this ground, and separately, Overthrust Belt oil and gas leasing has swept through the broader area in cycles since the 1970s. A single family's mineral history here can include both, an old coal lease from one generation and an oil and gas lease from another, on the same or adjacent land.
Before I quote you anything, I need to know which minerals your deed actually covers, because coal and oil and gas are priced through completely different mechanisms.

sections.heading: Coal country roots
paragraphs: Kemmerer's coal mining history predates most of the oil and gas leasing activity in this part of the state, and a lot of original land patents in the area reserved or conveyed coal rights separately from other minerals. If your deed specifically addresses coal, that's a different kind of asset than oil and gas, typically administered through longer-term royalty arrangements tied to mining volume.

sections.heading: Oil and gas leasing history
paragraphs: Separately, this area saw Overthrust Belt leasing pushes over the decades, mostly without production this close to Diamondville itself, since the belt's productive fields sit further east. Oil and gas interests here typically price as undeveloped, speculative acreage rather than anything currently producing.
I check the Lincoln County recorder's specific lease and deed history for your tract before saying which situation, coal, oil and gas, or both, applies to you.

Diamondville and Kemmerer have essentially grown together over the decades, and old deeds sometimes use one town name or the other interchangeably for the same legal description. That's not usually a problem for confirming ownership, but it's worth knowing before you assume a deed refers to a different tract than it actually does.

faqs.question: Do I own coal rights or oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Depends on your specific deed language. I'll review it and tell you clearly which mineral rights you hold.

faqs.question: Do you buy coal interests?
faqs.answer: My focus is oil and gas mineral interests. If your deed is coal-specific, I'll tell you plainly and point you toward what that would involve.

faqs.question: Has there been any oil and gas drilling right around Diamondville?
faqs.answer: Limited, if any, directly in town. I'll check your specific section's lease history before answering for your tract.

faqs.question: My deed says Kemmerer but I thought my land was near Diamondville. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. I'll match the legal description itself, section, township, range, rather than relying on the town name alone.
